content: {"summary":"Two logout waves occurred because the auth-service release changed session serialization, making sessions created before the release unreadable by the new version and sessions created during the release unreadable by the old version after rollback.","likely_cause":"Incompatible session serialization between old and new auth-service builds caused stranded sessions both forward and backward, producing two waves of AUTH‑E401X errors.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The first wave came from sessions created before the release, the second from sessions created while the release","evidence_ids":["INC-0178#0"],"quote":"first wave came from sessions created before the release, the second from sessions created while the release"},{"text":"Sessions written by the previous build could not be read by the new build, and vice‑versa, due to changed session serialization","evidence_ids":["INC-0178#1","RB-026#3"],"quote":"Sessions from before it can no longer be read"},{"text":"Rollback stranded sessions created between 14:08 and the rollback, causing the second wave of errors","evidence_ids":["INC-0178#2"],"quote":"Moving back stranded those created between 14:08 and the rollback"}],"next_checks":["Verify that future releases include backward‑compatible session readers before changing the writer","Confirm that Redis session data remained intact and was not corrupted during the rollout","Monitor AUTH‑E401X error rates per ReplicaSet to detect version‑specific issues early"]}
